newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech access lines grow 3.2 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech access lines grow 3.2 pct in Q1.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday its number of access lines in the first quarter of 1997 increased 3.2 percent versus last year, to 19.9 million.
The regional Bell telecommunications company said it posted 33 percent growth in cellular customers versus 1996, to 2.7 million subscribers.

Earlier, Ameritech reported first quarter earnings of $0.97 a share versus $0.86 a share last year, a 12.8 percent rise. Net rose 12.1 percent to $536 million from $478 million, making it the company's 14th consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth before one-time items, it said.

"Driven by strong customer demand, new services and entry into new markets, Ameritech is entering an era of greatly expanded opportunity," Richard Notebaert, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Ameritech said the first quarter growth was also fueled by a 50 percent annual increase in paging customers to 1.2 million and a 26 percent rise in sales of call management services such as Caller ID, call waiting and voice messaging.
The company said network access minutes of use rose 8.1 percent versus last year, and its number of security monitoring customers rose 12 percent to 444,000.

Ameritech's international businesses contributed more than one-fourth of the company's earnings growth, the company said. International investments include Belgacom SA of Belgium, MATAV of Hungary, Telecom Corp of New Zealand, NetCom of Norway, an alliance with ChinaCom to build cellular and landline networks in China, and WLW, a European business-to-business directory provider.

In addition, the company said its Americast cable television service expanded further during the first quarter. Ameritech added five cable TV franchises since the first of the year and now has 34 franchise agreements covering more than 1.7 million people. It is currently offering service in 22 communities in Illinois, Michigan and Ohio, the company said.
